text.p: Leading Greek club Olympiakos returned to form on Thursday, overwhelming Teamsystem Bologna 96-80 to restore their claim as one of the favourites in the re-vamped EuroLeague.

The Greeks recovered from last week's surprise home defeat by newcomers Alba Berlin to reassure the faithful with a non-stop show of aggression which helped maintain an average 10-point lead throughout.

Chicago Bulls hopeful Dragan Tarlac was the master of the boards sinking 29 points and pulling down 11 rebounds. American playmaker David Rivers produced his usual magic, darting past the Italian defence to add 18 points.

But the best news for the Greeks was a delightful display by NBA recruit Willy Anderson who ended with 13 points and was the home side's top blocker. Anderson seems to have adapted swiftly to European play after only two matches.
Bologna relied on mercurial playmaker Carlton Mayers who notched 28 points, including five triples.
Olympiakos, finalists in 1994 and 1995, are favourites for this season's title along with fellow Greeks and reigning champions Panathinaikos.
Pananthinaikos won their opening match last week but disappointed on Wednesday, losing in Spain 58-77 to Barcelona in a repeat of last season's final.
It was sweet revenge for Barcelona who have always argued they were robbed of the title by officials' errors.
